Inherited from Proto-Slavic *morka.

parole.significato: to trouble, to bother, to put out, to inconvenience
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *morčiti. By surface analysis, моро́ка (moróka) + -ити (-yty) and мо́рок (mórok) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *morьskъ. By surface analysis, мо́ре (móre, “sea”) + -ський (-sʹkyj). Compare Russian морско́й (morskój), Belarusian марскі́ (marskí), Polish morski.

parole.significato: to wrinkle, to pucker, to furrow, to crinkle, to crease, to rivel
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian мо́рщити (mórščiti), from Old East Slavic *мърщити (*mŭrščiti), from Proto-Slavic *mъrščiti.
From Proto-Slavic *mořakъ (by surface analysis, мо́ре (móre, “sea”) + -я́к (-ják)), from Proto-Slavic *moře, from Proto-Indo-European *móri, whence English marine and maritime.

parole.significato: to reel, to wind, to roll, to wrap
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *motati.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian мотыка (motyka), from Old East Slavic мотꙑка (motyka), from Proto-Slavic *motyka.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *motъloxъ, from the same roots as *loxъmotьje (whence Ukrainian лахмі́ття (laxmíttja), Russian лохмо́тья (loxmótʹja)).
From Proto-Slavic *motovǫzъ ("rope") from the combination of Proto-Slavic *motati ("to wind") and Proto-Slavic *vęzati ("to tie")
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mъxъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian мочи́ти (močíti), from Old East Slavic мочити (močiti), from Proto-Slavic *močiti. Causative of мо́кнути (móknuty).

parole.significato: midge (a kind of gnat or gnatlike fly)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mъši. Related to му́ха (múxa).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrьcь.
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *mьžuriti via metathesis, likely borrowed from Polish mrużyć. Doublet of жму́рити (žmúryty).

parole.significato: to loom (to appear indistinctly, e.g. when seen on the horizon or through the murk)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mьrěti.

Extended from earlier мрі́ти (mríty), from Proto-Slavic *mьrěti (compare Proto-Slavic *sěti → *sějati), from *mьr- + *-ěti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mir-, from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥-, from *mer- (“to shimmer, shine”). By surface analysis, мрі́ти (mríty) + -ати (-aty).

parole.significato: to take revenge, to retaliate, to avenge, to take vengeance, to wreak vengeance
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic мьстити (mĭstiti), from Proto-Slavic *mьstiti. Cognate with Russian мсти́ть (mstítʹ), Czech mstít, Polish mścić.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫdrьcь. By surface analysis, му́др(ий) (múdr(yj)) + -е́ць (-écʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫdrъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫdrostь. By surface analysis, му́дрий (múdryj, “wise”) + -ість (-istʹ). Compare Russian му́дрость (múdrostʹ), Belarusian му́драсць (múdrascʹ), Polish mądrość.
From Old East Slavic мѫжь (mǫžĭ), from Proto-Slavic *mǫžь.
From Proto-Slavic *mǫžьščina. Cognates include Russian мужчи́на (mužčína), Belarusian мужчы́на (mužčýna).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫka (“torture, torment”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǭka (“flour”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mulъ. Compare Polish muł, Serbo-Croatian му̑љ/mȗlj.
From Proto-Slavic *morvъ, from Proto-Indo-European *morwi- + -аха (-axa).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian мутити (mutiti), from Old East Slavic мꙋтити (mutiti), from Proto-Slavic *mǫtiti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mùxa.

parole.significato: to torture, to torment, to rack, to excruciate (inflict severe physical pain or mental suffering on)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mǫ̀čiti.

parole.significato: to rush (to take (someone/something) somewhere with great haste)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic *мъчати (*mŭčati), from Proto-Slavic *mъčati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mědь.

parole.significato: between, among (expressing position in space or time)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *meďu.

Inherited from Old East Slavic мѣзиньць (mězinĭcĭ, “youngest son”), from Proto-Slavic *mězinьcь. By surface analysis, мізи́нний (mizýnnyj) + -ець (-ecʹ). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic мѣзиньць (mězinĭcĭ, “youngest son”).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian мѣзиный (mězinyj), from Old East Slavic мѣзинъ (mězinŭ), from Proto-Slavic *mězinъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mojь.
From Old East Slavic мѣлъкъ (mělŭkŭ), from Proto-Slavic *mělъkъ.
Inherited from Old East Slavic моль (molĭ), from Proto-Slavic *moľь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měna.

parole.significato: to change, to alter, to modify
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měnìti (“to change, exchange”), from *měna (“change, exchange”).

parole.significato: to exchange, to trade, to barter (something or someone for something or someone)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian мѣнѧти, мѣнꙗти (měnjati, měnjati), from Old East Slavic мѣнѧти (měnęti), from Proto-Slavic *měňati. By surface analysis, мі́на (mína) + -яти (-jaty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měra.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian мѣрило (měrilo), from Old East Slavic мѣрило (měrilo), from Proto-Slavic *měridlo. By surface analysis, мі́рити (míryty) + -ло (-lo). Compare Russian мери́ло (merílo).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měriti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měsiti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *máiśīˀtei.
Inherited from Old East Slavic мостъ (mostŭ), from Proto-Slavic *mostъ (“bridge”).

parole.significato: to contain, to hold, to include (have within itself)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *městiti. Analyzable as мі́сто (místo) + -и́ти (-ýty). Cognate with Russian мести́ться (mestítʹsja), Polish mieścić.
Inherited from Middle Ukrainian мѣ́сто (místo), from Old East Slavic мѣ́сто (mě́sto), from Proto-Slavic *mě̀sto. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from Polish miasto.
From Proto-Slavic *měsęcь, from Proto-Indo-European *mḗh₁n̥s.
Inherited from Old East Slavic мѣтити (mětiti), from Proto-Slavic *mětiti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *metъla.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měxъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měxyrь. By surface analysis, міх (mix) + -ир (-yr).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měxurь. By surface analysis, міх (mix) + -ур (-ur).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *moťь. Doublet of міць (micʹ) and мо́щі (móšči).
Inherited from Old East Slavic мѣшати (měšati), from Proto-Slavic *měšati. Compare Russian меша́ть (mešátʹ), Belarusian мяша́ць (mjašácʹ), Polish mieszać.

parole.significato: sack (large bag for storage and handling; also the amount that can be put into this)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *měšьkъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *na.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *na.

parole.significato: to stuff, to pack [with instrumental ‘with something’] (to fill by packing or crowding; to fill closely or to repletion)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nabiti. Compare Russian наби́ть (nabítʹ), Belarusian набі́ць (nabícʹ), Polish nabić.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naborъ. By surface analysis, deverbal from набра́ти (nabráty). Compare Russian набо́р (nabór).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian навзнакъ (navznak), from на + взнакъ (na + vznak), from Proto-Slavic *vъznakъ. Cognate with Polish na wznak, Old Church Slavonic възнакъ (vŭznakŭ), Serbo-Croatian нȁузнāк, Russian на́взничь (návzničʹ).
From Proto-Slavic *naviděti, from *viděti. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyd-. Cognate with Czech náviděti, Polish nawidzieć.
From манити (manyty), which derived from Proto-Slavic *maniti, *manjǫ.
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *pólъ.

parole.significato: to go crazy, to go insane
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian навѣдити (navěditi, “to visit, (of God) to send down, to bring upon, to punish with, to inflict upon (trials, diseases, famine, etc.)”), from Old East Slavic навѣдити (navěditi, “to visit”), from Proto-Slavic *navěditi. The semantic narrowing (to inflict upon → to inflic
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nagъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian на́глый (náhlyj), from Old East Slavic наглъ (naglŭ), from Proto-Slavic *naglъ.

parole.significato: opportunity, chance, occasion (favorable circumstance for doing something)
parole.testo: Deverbal of obsolete нагоди́ти (nahodýty, “to happen to bring”), from Proto-Slavic *nagoditi (“to chance upon”). Compare Czech náhoda (“chance”).
Inherited from Old East Slavic надъ (nadŭ), from Proto-Slavic *nadъ.

parole.significato: to attract, to draw, to entice, to tempt, to allure
parole.testo: Most likely from Proto-Slavic *na (“on”) + Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put”), with the semantic shift: to put on → to hook, to bait (fish) → to attract, to allure. Compare a nearly identical formation: наді́ти (nadíty).

parole.significato: bowels of the earth, depths of the earth, subsoil
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nědra. Compare Russian не́дра (nédra).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naděja.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *najь, a contraction of *ne xaji (“do not touch”). Compare неха́й (nexáj).

parole.significato: prefix added to the comparative form of adjectives and adverbs to form the superlative form
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *najь-. From parts *na and particle *i. Approximates to prefix *nad-. Compare Russian наи- (nai-), Polish naj-, Serbo-Croatian naj-, Slovak naj- Slovene naj-, Czech nej-, Macedonian нај- (naj-), Bulgarian най- (naj-).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian найти́ (najtí), from Old East Slavic наити́ (naití), from Proto-Slavic *najьti. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + йти́ (jtý)

parole.significato: to belong (+ dative) (be the property of)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *naležati. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + лежа́ти (ležáty). Compare Belarusian нале́жаць (naljéžacʹ), Polish należeć, Russian належа́ть (naležátʹ).
From Proto-Slavic *nametъka. Related to мі́тити (mítyty). Cognate with Czech námětka, Russian наме́тка (namétka), Belarusian намётка (namjótka), Polish namiotka, Bulgarian наме́тка (namétka).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napadъ (“attack”). Synchronically, a deverbal from напада́ти (napadáty, “to attack”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napьrstъkъ. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + перст (perst, “finger”) + -ок (-ok).
From Proto-Slavic *napisati. Equivalent to на- (na-) + писа́ти (pysáty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napitъkъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *napojь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nareťi. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + ректи́ (rektý).
From Proto-Slavic *narodъ, perhaps via Russian народ (narod). The expected outcome, нарід (narid), is found dialectally.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodьnъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ. Doublet of наро́д (naród).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian наси́лье (nasílʹje), from Old East Slavic насилиѥ (nasilije), from Proto-Slavic *nasilьje. By surface analysis, на- (na-) + си́ла (sýla, “force”) + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: to force, to coerce, to compel
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian наси́ловати (nasílovati), from Old East Slavic насиловати (nasilovati), from Proto-Slavic *nasilovati. By surface analysis, на (na) + сила (syla) + -ува́ти (-uváty).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian наси́лникъ (nasílnik), from Old East Slavic насильникъ (nasilĭnikŭ), from Proto-Slavic *nasilьnikъ. By surface analysis, на (na) + си́ла (sýla, “force”) + -ник (-nyk).
на- (na-) + строїти (strojity), further from Proto-Slavic *strojiti. Cognate with Bulgarian настройвам (nastrojvam), Czech nastrojit (“arrange”), Russian настро́ить (nastróitʹ).

parole.significato: mood, humour, spirits, frame of mind, state of mind (mental or emotional state)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *nastrojь. By surface analysis, deverbal from настро́їти (nastrójity).

parole.significato: next, following (e.g., next Monday, next week, next month, next year)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *nastǫpiti, from Proto-Slavic *stǫpiti. Compare Czech nástupní and Polish następny.
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *tъlpa. Cognate with Belarusian натоўп (natówp); more distantly with Russian толпа́ (tolpá).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *našь.

parole.significato: descendant, offspring, progeny (person in relation to forebears)
parole.testo: From на- (na-) + ща́док (ščádok), from Proto-Slavic *sъčędъkъ or *ščędъkъ (compare Polish szczątek). Cognate with Belarusian нашча́дак (naščádak).
From Proto-Slavic *ne, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ne, from Proto-Indo-European *né.
From Middle Ukrainian небо (nebo), from Old East Slavic небо (nebo), from Proto-Slavic *nebo, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nébas, from Proto-Indo-European *nébʰos.
From Proto-Slavic *neboga. Cognate with Belarusian нябо́га (njabóha).
Back-formation from Proto-Slavic *nebože, vocative of *nebogъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevoľa. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + во́ля (vólja)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevodъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevědomъ. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + відо́мий (vidómyj). Compare Russian неве́домый (nevédomyj), Belarusian невядо́мы (njevjadómy).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevěrьnъ. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + ві́рний (vírnyj). Compare Russian неве́рный (nevérnyj), Belarusian няве́рны (njavjérny), Polish niewierny.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevěsta.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nedǫgъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *neděľa. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + діло (dilo) + -я (-ja)

parole.significato: rhinitis, runny nose, catarrh, coryza (inflammation of the nasal mucosa accompanied by secretions)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nežitъ. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + a deverbal from жи́ти (žýty). Compare Belarusian не́жыт (njéžyt), Polish nieżyt, Lithuanian niežas (“itching”).
Derived from Proto-Slavic *baviti. From не- (ne-) + за- (za-) + барити (baryty) + -ом (-om).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nemoťь. Compare Czech nemoc, Old Church Slavonic немощь (nemoštĭ), Serbo-Croatian не̏мо̄ћ. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + міч (mič).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nenaviděti. Cognates include Old Church Slavonic ненавидѣти (nenaviděti), Russian ненави́деть (nenavídetʹ), Belarusian ненаві́дзець (njenavídzjecʹ).
From Old East Slavic ненависть (nenavistĭ), from Proto-Slavic *nenavistь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nepravьda. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + пра́вда (právda). Compare Czech nepravda, Serbo-Croatian nepravda.
From Old East Slavic нерестъ (nerestŭ), from Proto-Slavic *nerstъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nérśtas.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nesti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *netopyřь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *neukъ. By surface analysis, не- (ne-) + ук (uk), combining form of учи́ти (učýty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ňiva.

parole.significato: to vegetate, to idle, to stagnate, to loaf, to do nothing
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ныдѣти (nyděti), from Proto-Slavic *nyděti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nižьnъ. Compare Russian ни́жний (nížnij).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nižьjь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nizъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian низа́ти (nizáti), from Old East Slavic низати (nizati), from Proto-Slavic *nizati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nizina.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian ни́зка (nízka), from Proto-Slavic *nizъka. By surface analysis, низ- (nyz-) + -ка (-ka).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian низкий (nizkij), from Old East Slavic низъкъ (nizŭkŭ), from Proto-Slavic *nizъkъ.

parole.significato: to sink, to prostrate, to droop, to sag, to lower oneself, to wilt
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian *никнꙋти (*niknuti), from Old East Slavic никнꙋти (niknuti), from Proto-Slavic *niknǫti.
Inherited from Old East Slavic нꙑнѣ (nyně), from Proto-Slavic *nyně, from Proto-Indo-European *nu (“now”).
Inherited from Old East Slavic нꙑрꙗти, нирати (nyrjati, nirati), from Proto-Slavic *nyřati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nyti (“to yearn”).
From Middle Ukrainian нить (nytʹ), from Old East Slavic нить (nitĭ), from Proto-Slavic *nitь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nī́ˀtis, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)neh₁-.

parole.significato: low, despicable, dirty, abject, scummy, vile
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ниць (nicʹ), from Old East Slavic ниць (nicĭ), from Proto-Slavic *nicь.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian ниць (nicʹ), from Old East Slavic ниць (nicĭ), the fossilized indefinite masculine nominative singular of Proto-Slavic *nicь, whence also Old East Slavic and Old Ruthenian ниць (nicʹ) and Ukrainian ни́ций (nýcyj).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *niščь.

parole.significato: used to soften a command and/or to indicate a recommendation
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nъ, related to ну (nu) and ни́ні (nýni)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nòvъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néwos, with -ий (-yj).
Inherited from Old East Slavic нога (noga), from Proto-Slavic *noga.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nora.
From Proto-Slavic *nositi, iterative form of *nesti (whence also нести́ (nestý)).

parole.significato: a kind of tub used for performing household jobs, particularly bathing small children and kneading dough
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic ночьвы (nočĭvy), from Proto-Slavic *nъťьvy.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nu, from Proto-Indo-European *nu.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian нꙋдити (nuditi), from Old East Slavic нꙋдити (nuditi), from Proto-Slavic *nuditi. By surface analysis, ну́да́ (núdá) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian нꙋдны́й (nudnýj, “boring”), from Old East Slavic нꙋдьнъ (nudĭnŭ, “gruelling, difficult”), from Proto-Slavic *nudьnъ. By surface analysis, ну́да́ (núdá) + -ний (-nyj).

parole.significato: to say "ну" ("nu") continually (in expressions of inducement, incitement, encouragement; to impel, drive on incite)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian *нꙋкати (*nukati) (attested in понꙋкати (ponukati)), from Proto-Slavic *nukati. By surface analysis, ну (nu) + -кати (-katy).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ňuxъ, itself of uncertain origin.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ňuxati.

From Proto-Slavic *ňaňa, a reduplicated nursery formation. Similar nursery formations are widespread in Proto-Indo-European; compare Sanskrit नना (nanā́, “mother”), Ancient Greek νάννα (nánna, “aunt”), Albanian nënë (“mother”), Welsh nain (“grandmother”).
From Proto-Slavic *ni, from Proto-Indo-European *néy.

parole.significato: A prefix used to derive negative forms of interrogative adverbs, determiners, and pronouns: no-
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ni-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nogъtь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nikъde. By surface analysis, ні (ni) + де (de). Cognate with Russian нигде́ (nigdé), Belarusian нідзе́ (nidzjé), Polish nigdzie.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nožь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *něžiti, from *něga. By surface analysis, нíга (níha) + -ити (-yty). Compare Russian не́жить (néžitʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *něžьnъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nozdra.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian николи (nikoli, “never”), from Old East Slavic николи (nikoli, “never”), from Proto-Slavic *nikoli (“never”). By surface analysis, ні- (ni-) + коли (koly). Cognate with Belarusian ніко́лі (nikóli), Old Church Slavonic николи, николиже (nikoli, nikoliže) and Slovene nikọ̑
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nikǫda. By surface analysis, ні- (ni-) + куди (kudy). Cognate with Russian не́куда (nékuda), Belarusian некуды́ (njekudý).
From Proto-Slavic *němьcь (“foreigner, German”), from *němъ (“mute”). Cognate with Ukrainian німи́й (nimýj).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *němьčьskъ, from Proto-Slavic *němьcь. By surface analysis, Ні́меччина (Nímeččyna) + -цький (-cʹkyj).
From Old East Slavic нѣмъ (němŭ), from Proto-Slavic *němъ + -ий (-yj)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *němota. By surface analysis, німи́й (nimýj) + -ота (-ota).

parole.significato: to become dumb, to become mute, to become speechless
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *něměti, from *němъ + *-ěti. By surface analysis, німи́й (nimýj) + -і́ти (-íty). Compare Russian неме́ть (nemétʹ), Belarusian няме́ць (njamjécʹ), Polish niemieć.
From Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s.

From Proto-Slavic *nikъto. By surface analysis, univerbation of ні (ni) + хто (xto). Cognates include Belarusian ніхто́ (nixtó), Russian никто́ (niktó) and Polish nikt. Parsable as ні- (ni-) + хто (xto).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ničьjь (“nobody's”). By surface analysis, univerbation of ні (ni) + чий (čyj). Cognate with Russian ниче́й (ničéj), Belarusian нічый (ničyj). Parsable as ні- (ni-) + чий (čyj).

Inherited from Old East Slavic ночьлѣгъ (nočĭlěgŭ), from Proto-Slavic *noťьlěgъ. Equivalent to ніч (nič, “night”) + лежа́ти (ležáty). Compare Russian ночле́г (nočlég), Belarusian начле́г (načljéh), Polish nocleg, Czech nocleh, Slovak nocľah.

Inherited from Old East Slavic ничьто (ničĭto), from Proto-Slavic *ničьto. By surface analysis, univerbation of ні (ni, “not”) + що (ščo, “what”). Compare Belarusian нішто́ (ništó), Russian ничто́ (ništó) and Polish nic. Parsable as ні- (ni-) + що (ščo).

parole.significato: in no way, not in a way, nowise
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nijako (“in no way”). by surface analysis, univerbation of ні (ni) + як (jak). Compare Russian ника́к (nikák), Belarusian нія́к (niják), Polish nijak. Parsable as ні- (ni-) + як (jak).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nijakъ (“neither, none”). By surface analysis, univerbation of ні (ni) + яки́й (jakýj). Compare Russian никако́й (nikakój), Belarusian нія́кі (nijáki), Polish nijaki. Parsable as ні- (ni-) + який (jakyj).

parole.significato: prefix added to adjectives or nouns to produce factitive verbs in conjunction with -ити (-iti), i.e. verbs with the mea…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *o(b), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ebʰi.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ob.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *oba.

parole.significato: outline (a line marking the boundary of an object figure)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obvodъ. By surface analysis, a deverbal from обво́дити (obvódyty). Russian обво́д (obvód), Belarusian абво́д (abvód), Polish obwód.

parole.significato: to revolve, to rotate, to spin, to turn, to turn round
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian оберта́ти (obertáti), from Proto-Slavic *obvьrtati. By surface analysis, об- (ob-) + верта́ти (vertáty). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian о̀бртати/òbrtati.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian обадва (obadva), from Old East Slavic оба два (oba dva), from Proto-Slavic *oba dъva. By surface analysis, univerbation of оба́ (obá) + два (dva).

From Old East Slavic обличье (obličĭje), from Proto-Slavic *obličьje, from *oblikъ + *-ьje, from *ob- + *likъ + -я (-ja). Cognate with Russian обли́чье (oblíčʹje), Belarusian аблі́чча (ablíčča), Polish oblicze, Czech obličej.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian облу́да (oblúda, “ghost, deception, pretense, temptation”), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *luditi (“to deceive, to delude”).

parole.significato: to apotheosize, to deify, to divinize
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bogovati. Cognate with Russian обожать (obožatʹ), Serbo-Croatian обожавати.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obolkъ.
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *bòlna (“membrane”).
From Proto-Slavic *bornь. Related to брань (branʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obrazъ.

parole.significato: to insult, to offend, to abuse, to affront
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *obraziti. Analyzable as об- (ob-) + ра́зити (rázyty). Compare Belarusian абра́зіць (abrázicʹ), Polish obrazić.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obrusъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obrędъ.

parole.significato: to edge, to border, to trim
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obšiti. By surface analysis, об- (ob-) + шити (šyty). Cognate to Polish obszyć, Russian обшить (obšitʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obědъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obvodъ. Compare Russian о́бод (óbod).

parole.significato: to have lunch, to lunch, to have dinner (eat a midday meal)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic обѣдати (obědati), from Proto-Slavic *obědati, from *obědъ + *-ati, ultimately from *ěsti (“to eat”). Equivalent to обі́д (obíd) + -ати (-aty). Compare Russian обе́дать (obédatʹ), Belarusian абе́даць (abjédacʹ).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian обойма́ти (obojmáti), from Old East Slavic объимати (obŷimati), from Proto-Slavic *obъjьmati. By surface analysis, обі- (obi-) + -йма́ти (-jmáty). Compare Belarusian абыйма́ць (abyjmácʹ), Russian обнима́ть (obnimátʹ).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian *обосра́ти (*obosráti), from Old East Slavic *объсьрати (*obŭsĭrati), from Proto-Slavic *o(b)sьrati. By surface analysis, обі- (obi-) + сра́ти (sráty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ovьsъ.
Inherited from Old East Slavic овочь (ovočĭ, “fruit”), from Proto-Slavic *ovoťe.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian огоро́жа (ohoróža), from Proto-Slavic *ogorďa. By surface analysis, огороди́ти (ohorodýty) + -а (-a).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *odeďa.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian оди́нъ (odín), from Proto-Slavic *edinъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *edьnostajьnъ. Compare Belarusian аднаста́йны (adnastájny), Polish jednostajny, Czech jednostejný.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian оди́нъ (odín), from Proto-Slavic *edinъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *edinъ na desęte.

parole.significato: glaze, glaze ice, glazed frost, verglas, sleet
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *o(b)želdь, from Proto-Slavic *o(b)- + *želdь. Cognate with Kashubian żłódz and Polish żłód.
From Proto-Slavic *ežina; cognate with Polish jeżyna and Belarusian ажы́на (ažýna).
From Proto-Slavic *ȅzero, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *éźeran.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian о́ко (óko), from Proto-Slavic *oko.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian *окраина (*okraina), from Old East Slavic *окраина (*okraina), from Proto-Slavic *o(b)krajina. By surface analysis, о- (o-) + край (kraj) + -ина (-yna).
Most likely ultimately from Proto-Slavic *kroma.
Inherited from Old East Slavic округъ (okrugŭ), from Proto-Slavic *okrǫgъ, from *ob- + *krǫgъ (“circle”).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian ꙋкропъ (ukrop, “hot water”), from Old East Slavic ꙋкропъ (ukropŭ, “hot water”), from Proto-Slavic *ukropъ. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic оукропъ (ukropŭ, “hot soup”) and Czech úkrop (“garlic soup”).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian о́кунь (ókunʹ), from Old East Slavic о́кунь (ókunĭ), from Proto-Slavic *òkunь. Cognate with Polish okoń, Belarusian акунь (akunʹ), Czech okoun, Slovak okún, Bulgarian окун (okun), Serbo-Croatian окун.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *elỳ.

parole.significato: tin (attributive) (of, pertaining to, or made of tin)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic оловѧнꙑи (olovęnyi), оловѣнꙑи (olověnyi), from Proto-Slavic *olověnъ, *olověnьnъ, from *olovo (“lead”) + *-ěnъ. Equivalent to о́лово (ólovo) + -я́ний (-jányj). Compare Russian оловя́нный (olovjánnyj), Belarusian алавя́ны (alavjány), Polish ołowiany (“lead, leaden”).
From Proto-Slavic *olovo (“lead”).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian олѣ́й (olě́j, “olive oil, vegetable oil”), from Old East Slavic олѣи (olěi, “olive oil”), from Proto-Slavic *olějь, from Ancient Greek ἔλαιον (élaion) or Latin oleum. Doublet of єле́й (jeléj) Cognate with Belarusian алей (aljej), Bulgarian елей (elej), Lower Sorbian wole

parole.significato: inula, elecampane (Inula spp., especially Inula helenium)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *omanъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *emela.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *onъde.
Inherited from Old East Slavic вънукъ (vŭnukŭ), from Proto-Slavic *vъnukъ.

parole.significato: footwrap (strip of cloth worn around the feet)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *onuťa. Cognate with Polish onuca.
Derived from Proto-Slavic *pęta (“heel”) (with о- (o-) prefix). Cognates include Czech opět, Old Polish opięć, Russian опя́ть (opjátʹ), Serbo-Croatian opet.

parole.significato: to find oneself, to end up (discover oneself to be in a particular place; get somewhere unexpectedly or by happenstance)
parole.testo: From опини́ти (opynýty) + -ся (-sja), from о- (o-) + пини́ти (pynýty), from Proto-Slavic *pin(ati) + -ити (-yty), from Proto-Slavic *pęti.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian опытъ (opyt), from Old East Slavic опꙑтъ (opytŭ), from Proto-Slavic *o(b)pytъ. Deverbal from опита́ти, опи́тувати (opytáty, opýtuvaty)
Apparently derived from Proto-Slavic *polnъ (“barren”). Cognate with Belarusian пало́нка (palónka).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *o(b)pora.

parole.significato: custodian, guardian (a person entrusted with the custody or care of something or someone; someone who guards, watches o…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian опеку́нъ (opekún), from Proto-Slavic *opekunъ. By surface analysis, опік(а́ти) (opik(áty)) + -у́н (-ún).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *oradlo. By surface analysis, ора́ти (oráty) + -ло (-lo).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian ора́ти (oráti), from Old East Slavic орати (orati), from Proto-Slavic *oràti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *árˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éryeti, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erh₃-.
From Old East Slavic орьлъ (orĭlŭ), from Proto-Slavic *orьlъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *arélis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃érō.

parole.significato: to manage, to control, to govern (with instrumental)
parole.testo: From ору́ддя (orúddja, “gear”) + -увати (-uvaty), from Proto-Slavic *orǫdьje.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian орꙋже (oruže), from Old East Slavic орѫжие (orǫžije), from Proto-Slavic *orǫžьje.
From Proto-Slavic *osa, from Proto-Indo-European *wobʰseh₂.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *osьlъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *esetrъ.
From Old East Slavic основа (osnova), from Proto-Slavic *osnova.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian оста́нный (ostánnyj), from Proto-Slavic *ostanьnъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ostrovъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *esenь.

parole.significato: there, here, now. Used demonstratively to point to something in space or time.
parole.testo: Proto-Slavic *otъ, from the Proto-Slavic demonstrative stem Proto-Slavic *t- (cf. той (toj), тут (tut)).

parole.significato: aftergrass, aftermath; grass that comes up after mowing
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *otava.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *otъvorъ. Compare Polish otwór, Czech otvor, Serbo-Croatian о̀твор/òtvor.
From Old East Slavic отьць (otĭcĭ), from Proto-Slavic *otьcь, from Proto-Indo-European *átta.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *oxota.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ocьtъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian *очере́тъ (*očerét), from Old East Slavic очеретъ (očeretŭ), from Proto-Slavic *o(b)čertъ.
From Proto-Slavic *pьjavъka. Cognate with Russian пия́вка (pijávka), Belarusian п'я́ўка (pʺjáwka), Polish pijawka.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьjanъ.

parole.significato: to stick out, to thrust out
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian *пѧти (*pjati), from Old East Slavic пѧти (pęti), from Proto-Slavic *pęti (“to stretch”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pęta.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pętь desęti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pętъ.
From Old East Slavic пѧть (pętĭ), from Proto-Slavic *pętь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pa-.
From Old East Slavic паукъ (paukŭ), from Proto-Slavic *paǫkъ, from *pa- + *ǫkъ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enkos (“hook”).
From Proto-Slavic *paǫčina; morphologically, from паву́к (pavúk) + -ина (-yna).
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *gъnati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *padati.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian падежъ (padež), from Old East Slavic падежь (padežĭ), from Proto-Slavic *padežь. By surface analysis, пад- (pad-) + -іж (-iž). Cognate with Russian падёж (padjóž), Bulgarian паде́ж (padéž), Serbo-Croatian па́деж, Old Church Slavonic падежь (padežĭ).
Inherited from Old East Slavic пазъ (pazŭ), from Proto-Slavic *pazъ.

parole.significato: to observe, to watch, to keep an eye on
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paziti or, considering its spread, likely borrowed from Romanian păzi, from Old Church Slavonic пазити (paziti).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pazurъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pazduxa.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pakъ.

parole.significato: to blaze, to flame, to be ablaze, to be aflame
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *palati, frequentative of *polěti. Compare Belarusian пала́ць (palácʹ), Polish pałać.

parole.significato: finger (digit of the hand, including the thumb)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic пальць (palĭcĭ), from Proto-Slavic *palьcь (“thumb, finger”).

parole.significato: to burn (to cause to be consumed by fire)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paliti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *palica.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *palъka.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *palubъ. By surface analysis, па- (pa-) + луб (lub, “bast”) + -а (-a). Cognate with Czech paluba, Polish pałuba, pałub.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian памѧта́ти (pamjatáti), from Proto-Slavic *pamętati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pamętьnъ. Compare Russian па́мятный (pámjatnyj), Belarusian па́мятны (pámjatny), Polish pamiętny.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pamętь.
Inherited from Old East Slavic папьрть (papĭrtĭ), from Proto-Slavic *papьrtь, from *pa- + *pьrtь (“front”). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic папръть (paprŭtĭ), Bulgarian папрът (paprăt).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paportь.
From Proto-Slavic *para, *parъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian па́рити (páriti), from Old East Slavic парити (pariti), from Proto-Slavic *pariti. By surface analysis, па́ра (pára, “steam”) + -ити (-yty).

parole.significato: to soar, to glide, to plane
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian пари́ти (paríti), from Old East Slavic парити (pariti), from Proto-Slavic *pariti.

parole.significato: a boy about to become a young man
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paõrbę. Equivalent to па- (pa-) + Old East Slavic робъ (robŭ, “slave”) + -'я (-ʺja).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paorbъkъ. Equivalent to па- (pa-) + Old East Slavic робъ (robŭ, “slave”) + -ок (-ok).

parole.significato: stepson (son of one's spouse, but not one's own child)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pasynъkъ.

parole.significato: bastard, scumbag, asshole, piece of shit
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paskǫda.

parole.significato: to graze, to pasture, to shepherd
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pasti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pàsti.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian пастыръ (pastyr), from Old East Slavic пастꙑрь (pastyrĭ), from Proto-Slavic *pastyřь.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian пасту́хъ (pastúx), from Old East Slavic пастухъ (pastuxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *pastuxъ. By surface analysis, пасти́ (pastý) + -ух (-ux).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pastь.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian па́сѣка (pásěka), from Proto-Slavic *pasěka. By surface analysis, па- (pa-) + сікти́ (siktý) + -а (-a). Compare Belarusian па́сека (pásjeka), Polish pasieka.

parole.significato: to look at, to watch, to stare at, to eye
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *patrati.
Inherited from Old East Slavic пахъ (paxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *paxъ. Cognate with Russian пах (pax) and Polish pacha.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian паха́ти (paxáti), from Old East Slavic пахати (paxati), from Proto-Slavic *paxati. Sense 2 is likely from Russian паха́ть (paxátʹ, “to slave away”).
Possibly inherited from Proto-Slavic *paxъve, genitive of *paxу. Related to пах (pax, “groin”). Compare Polish pacha.

parole.significato: to smell (of/like something: + instrumental case), to be fragrant
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *paxnǫti.
From Proto-Slavic [Term?]. Cognate with Belarusian пацу́к (pacúk), Russian пасю́к (pasjúk).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pacę, onomatopoeic in origin.

parole.significato: Grass used as feed for livestock.
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic паша (paša) from Proto-Slavic *paša. Related to Proto-Slavic *pasti (“to pasture”). Cognate with Polish pasza, Czech paša, Slovak paša, Serbo-Croatian pȁša, and Slovene páša.

parole.significato: mouth, maw, jaws (of an animal, reptile or fish)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *pastь, altered by analogy with паще́ка (paščéka).

Inherited from Old East Slavic паꙗти (pajati, “to forge”). Cognate with Russian пая́ть (pajátʹ), Belarusian пая́ць (pajácʹ), Czech pájet. Probably related to пої́ти (pojíty) (from Proto-Slavic *pojiti) and thereby to Old Church Slavonic съпоити (sŭpoiti), Serbo-Croatian спо̀јити/spòjiti, Slovene spo

Inherited from Old Ruthenian пе́кло (péklo, “hell”), from Old East Slavic пькълъ (pĭkŭlŭ, “pitch, tar, resin”), from Proto-Slavic *pьkъlo (“pitch, tar, resin”). The meaning "hell" is a semantic loan from Old Polish piekło, which arose under the Christian influence (sinners are submerged in boiling t

Inherited from Old Ruthenian пекти (pekti), from Old East Slavic печи (peči), from Proto-Slavic *peťi; the -kt- cluster, which had regularly become -ť- before -i in Proto-Slavic, was restored by analogy.

parole.significato: hemline, hem, lap (the line formed by the bottom edge of a skirt, dress, or coat)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian пелена (pelena), from Old East Slavic пелена (pelena), from Proto-Slavic *pelena.
From Old East Slavic пьнь (pĭnĭ), from Proto-Slavic *pь̏ňь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьrga.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pьrděti.

parole.significato: over, over again (describing an action of moving by overcoming one or more obstacles)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *per-.

parole.significato: to kill, to slay (all of many of, one after another)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *perbiti. By surface analysis, пере- (pere-) + би́ти (býty). Compare Russian переби́ть (perebítʹ), Belarusian перабі́ць (pjerabícʹ).

parole.significato: to transport, to carry, to convey, to haul, to shift
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pervezti. By surface analysis, пере- (pere-) + везти́ (veztý)

parole.significato: humus (a large group of natural organic compounds, found in the soil, formed from the chemical and biological decomposi…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pergnojь. By surface analysis, deverbal from перегни́ти (perehnýty). Compare Russian перегно́й (peregnój), Belarusian перагно́й (pjerahnój).

parole.significato: just before, in front of (expressing position in space or time)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic передъ (peredŭ), from Proto-Slavic *perdъ.
From Old East Slavic передъ- (peredŭ-), from Proto-Slavic *perdъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *perdьnъ. By surface analysis, пере́д (peréd) + -ній (-nij).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian перезъ (perez), from Old East Slavic перезъ (perezŭ), from Proto-Slavic *perzъ. Doublet of през (prez).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *perlomъ.

Uncertain. Possibly from Proto-Slavic *stydnǫti or related to Lithuanian stū́gti (“to harden, to stiffen”). Cognate with Russian сты́нуть (stýnutʹ), Belarusian сты́гнуць (stýhnucʹ), Polish stygnąć.

parole.significato: to stick out, to jut out, to protrude, to project

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъtiskati. Compare Belarusian сціска́ць (sciskácʹ), Polish ściskać.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъto.
From Proto-Slavic *stъlpъ, a form of *stъlbъ.

parole.significato: to groan, to wail, to weep, to moan
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian стогна́ти (stohnáti), from Old East Slavic стонати (stonati), from Proto-Slavic *stonati. The "г" is probably of expressive origin, compare Old East Slavic стогнание (stognanije).

parole.significato: capital (city designated as seat of government)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stolica. By surface analysis, стіл (stil) + -иця (-ycja).
From Proto-Slavic *stopa, from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to stand still”). See also Russian стопа́ (stopá), Polish stopa; akin to Lithuanian stapytis.
From Old East Slavic сторожь (storožĭ), from Proto-Slavic *storžь (“guard”). Doublet of страж (straž).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *storna.
Inherited from Old East Slavic стоꙗти (stojati), from Proto-Slavic *stojati.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stradati. Compare Russian страда́ть (stradátʹ).

parole.significato: church service during the evening of the Maundy Thursday
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strastь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *straxъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strašidlo. By surface analysis, страшити (strašyty) + -ло (-lo)
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strašiti. By surface analysis, страх (strax) + -и́ти (-ýty).
From Proto-Slavic *strašьnъ. Equivalent to страх (strax) + -ний (-nyj). Compare Russian стра́шный (strášnyj), Belarusian стра́шны (strášny), Polish straszny, Serbo-Croatian strašan.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stremę.

parole.significato: to jump, to leap, to bound, to spring, to skip
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strybati.

parole.significato: to cut (hair, fur, grass, etc.), to shear, to clip, to trim
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *striťi.

parole.significato: rod, bar, shank (long, straight, narrow object)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic стрьжьнъ (strĭžĭnŭ), from Proto-Slavic *strьžьnь (“core; nucleus; pivotal part”). Melnychuk posits a connection with Swedish streke for the sense 'deep stream'.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strъjь.

parole.significato: to stick out, to jut out, to protrude, to project
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strьměti. Doublet of стремі́ти (stremíty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strogъ.
Inherited from Old East Slavic сърокъ (sŭrokŭ), from Proto-Slavic *sъrokъ.

parole.significato: motley, variegated (having many colours; streaked, spotted or otherwise marked with a variety of colour)
parole.testo: Melnychuk posits derivation from a Proto-Slavic etymon meaning "covered with dots, lines or stripes" (cf. Proto-Slavic *stroka). Alternatively from Proto-Slavic *sorka (“magpie”) (whence соро́ка (soróka)). Compare Belarusian страка́ты (strakáty), Polish strokaty, pstrokaty, srokaty, Czech and Slovak

parole.significato: to insert, to stick, to put
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian строми́ти (stromíti, “to direct (gaze)”), from Proto-Slavic *stromiti, with the semantic shift: to direct → to drive, to propel → to stab, to stick, to impale. Most likely related or parallel to стремі́ти (stremíty). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic стрьмлениѥ (strĭmleni
from Proto-Slavic *strojiti.
Inherited from Old East Slavic стругъ (strugŭ), from Proto-Slavic *strugъ. Compare Bulgarian струг (strug), Old Church Slavonic строугъ (strugŭ), Slovene strȗg, Czech struh, Polish strug.

parole.significato: to plane, to whittle, to adze, to shave (to remove thin slices off wood, metal, etc., with a sharp tool)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian стрꙋга́ти (struháti), from Proto-Slavic *strugati.

parole.significato: stream, spurt, squirt, jet, spout (of liquid)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian струмень (strumenʹ), from Proto-Slavic *strumy. By surface analysis, струм (strum) + -інь m (-inʹ).

parole.significato: string (segment of wire or other material used as vibrating element on a musical instrument)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *struna.
Derived from Proto-Slavic *struna.
Inherited from Old East Slavic струпъ (strupŭ), from Proto-Slavic *strupъ.

parole.significato: to get stuck, to stick, to get bogged down (in)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strojь.

From Old East Slavic стрѣлꙗти (strěljati), from Proto-Slavic *strěľati.

parole.significato: steep, abrupt, precipitous, sharp, sheer (of a near-vertical gradient)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *stromъ. With -кий (-kyj) suffix.

Probably, from earlier стрі́ти (stríty), remodeled after its present tense forms (e.g. стрі́ну, стрі́нуть (strínu, strínutʹ)) by analogy with verbs suffixed with -ну́ти (-núty). Or maybe, considering Czech střetnout and Old Czech střětnúti, inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъrětьnǫti.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian стрѣ́ти (strě́ti), from Proto-Slavic *sъrěsti.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian стрѣ́тити (strě́titi), from Old East Slavic стрѣтити (strětiti), from Proto-Slavic *sъrětiti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strěxa. Cognate with Belarusian страха́ (straxá), Polish strzecha and Serbo-Croatian strèha.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *studiti.

parole.significato: to knock, to bang, to rap, to tap (to make a sharp noise by striking something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stukati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stǫpati. Compare Russian ступа́ть (stupátʹ), Belarusian ступа́ць (stupácʹ), Polish stąpać.
From Proto-Slavic *stǫpiti, from Proto-Indo-European *stab- (“to support”). Compare Russian ступи́ть (stupítʹ), Belarusian ступі́ць (stupícʹ), Polish stąpnąć.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stǫpenь.
Formed from Proto-Slavic *vъstǫga.
From Middle Ukrainian стогъ (stoh), from Proto-Slavic *stogъ.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian столецъ (stolecʹ, “chair”), from Old East Slavic стольць (stolĭcĭ, “chair”), from Proto-Slavic *stolьcь. By surface analysis, стіл (stil) + -ець (-ecʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stěna.

parole.significato: com-, con- (forms nouns denoting a connection or link)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sǫglobъ, *sъglobъ. Cognate with Bulgarian сглоб (sglob), Serbo-Croatian згло̏б/zglȍb.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sǫdakъ.
From Proto-Slavic *sǫdì + -я (-ja).

parole.significato: vessel (tube or canal that carries fluid in an animal or plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *sǫdъ, identical to the origin of суд (sud, “court”), with -и́на (-ýna) suffix. Compare Russian сосу́д (sosúd).

parole.significato: to judge, to try, to adjudicate
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sǫditi.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian сꙋдьба (sudʹba, “judgment, fate”), from Old East Slavic сѫдьба, сꙋдьба (sǫdĭba, sudĭba), from Proto-Slavic *sǫdьba. By surface analysis, суд- (sud-) + -ьба́ (-ʹbá).
Inherited from Old East Slavic сука (suka), from Proto-Slavic *sùka, further etymology unclear.

parole.significato: to strand, to twist, to twine, to weave
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian сꙋка́ти (sukáti), from Proto-Slavic *sukati.

parole.significato: cloth, broadcloth (a dense, smooth woolen or (rarely) cotton fabric)

parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic. Cognate with Russian сумя́тица (sumjática), Belarusian сумятня́ (sumjatnjá). By surface analysis, су- (su-) + м'яти (mʺjaty) + -я (-ja).
Inherited from Old East Slavic суморок (sumorok), from Proto-Slavic *sǫmorkъ. Doublet of су́мрак (súmrak).

parole.significato: to shove in, to put (in), to stick in
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic сꙋнꙋти (sunuti), from Proto-Slavic *sunǫti. Cognate with Belarusian су́нуць (súnucʹ), Russian су́нуть (súnutʹ), Serbo-Croatian су́нути, Czech sunout, Polish sunąć,.
From Old East Slavic супьрьникъ (supĭrĭnikŭ), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *sǫ-, *perti (“to beat, press up, balk”). Compare Russian сопе́рник (sopérnik). Featuring -ник (-nyk) suffix.

parole.significato: to furrow (eyebrows), to wrinkle (forehead) (in displeasure, vexation)

Inherited from Old East Slavic супостатъ (supostatŭ), from Proto-Slavic *sǫpostatъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sǫprǫgъ.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *surovъ.

parole.significato: neighbor (a person living on adjacent or nearby land)

From Old East Slavic соуть (sutĭ), from Proto-Slavic *sǫtь.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *suxъ.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sidlo. Doublet of (obsolete) сило́ (syló), whence сильце́ (sylʹcé).

Inherited from Old East Slavic сельскъіи (selĭskyi), from Proto-Slavic *sèlьskъ. By surface analysis, село́ (seló, “village”) + -ськи́й (-sʹkýj, adjective-forming suffix). Cognate with Belarusian се́льскі (sjélʹski) and Russian се́льский (sélʹskij).
From Proto-Slavic *sedmь, from Proto-Indo-European *septḿ̥.

From Old East Slavic сѣмиꙗ (sěmija), from Proto-Slavic *sěmьja.

parole.significato: family (group of people who are closely related to one another)

parole.significato: a town that was part of the greater sich (Січ)
parole.testo: Deverbal from сі́кти (síkty), from Proto-Slavic *sěťi, from Proto-Indo-European *sek-.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian сѣꙗти (sějati, “to sift, to sieve”), from Proto-Slavic *sějati (“to sift, to sieve”).

From Proto-Slavic *tata, compare Russian тата (tata).

From Old East Slavic тварь (tvarĭ, “item, object, creation”), from Proto-Slavic *tvarь.
Inherited from Old East Slavic твьрдъ (tvĭrdŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *twírˀtas, from Proto-Indo-European *twerH-. Doublet of кварц (kvarc).

parole.significato: to affirm, to assert, to aver, to claim, to insist, to maintain (state emphatically)

From Old East Slavic тверезъ (tverezŭ), a metathesised form of терезвъ (terezvŭ), from Proto-Slavic *terzvъ.

parole.significato: creator, maker (something or someone which creates or makes something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tvorьcь. By surface analysis, твори́ти (tvorýty) + -ець (-ecʹ). Compare Old Church Slavonic творьць (tvorĭcĭ), Russian творе́ц (tvoréc), Belarusian тварэ́ц (tvaréc), Polish twórca.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tvoriti.

parole.significato: your, yours, thy, thine (2nd-person familiar, singular only)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic твои (tvoi), from Proto-Slavic *tvojь.

parole.significato: A person sharing their first name or surname with another; a namesake.
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *tьzъ.

parole.significato: to flow, to run, to stream, to move

parole.significato: net (a mesh of string, cord or rope, used for trapping animals)

From теребити (terebyty) + -івля (-ivlja). Inherited from Proto-Slavic *terbiti (“to clear from planting, to tear”).

parole.significato: tower, tower-room; a living area in a building or upper part of a building in the shape of a tower, especially in ancie…
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *termъ. Cognate with Serbo-Croatian trijem/тријем.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tьrnъ.

parole.significato: to torment, to torture, to anguish, to excruciate, to harrow
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic тьрзати (tĭrzati), from Proto-Slavic *tьrzati. Due to its literary nature, it was possibly borrowed from Old Church Slavonic трьзати (trĭzati).

From терни́ (terný) + -и́стий (-ýstyj). Compare Russian терни́стый (ternístyj), Belarusian цярні́сты (cjarnísty), Polish ciernisty. The root is inherited from Proto-Slavic *tьrnъ (“thorn, blackthorn”).

parole.significato: to endure, to suffer, to tolerate, to stand
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic тьрпѣти (tĭrpěti), from Proto-Slavic *tьrpěti.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian тесакъ (tesak), from Proto-Slavic *tesakъ. By surface analysis, теса́ти (tesáty) + -ак (-ak). Cognate with Czech tesák and Polish ciesak, ciosak.

parole.significato: to chop away the surface level (with a sharp tool)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic (see *tesàti and *tesla). By surface analysis, тесло́ (tesló) + -я́р (-jár).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tьstь.
Inherited from Old East Slavic тета (teta), from Proto-Slavic *teta.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tьšča.
From Proto-Slavic *ty, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tūˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *túh₂.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъjьžedьnь.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian ты́кати (týkati), from Old East Slavic тыкати (tykati), from Proto-Slavic *tykati. Cognates include Bulgarian ти́кам (tíkam), Czech týkat.

parole.significato: Lagenaria, calabash, bottle gourd (plant and fruit)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ты́ква (týkva), ти́ква (tíkva), from Old East Slavic тꙑкꙑ (tyky), from Proto-Slavic *tyky.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tylъ.

parole.significato: fence made out of vines and branches; wattle
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic тꙑнъ (tynŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tynъ. Cognate with Belarusian and Russian тын (tyn), Polish tyn, and further with German Zaun, English town.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tisъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tiskati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tisnǫti or *tisknǫti. Compare Russian ти́снуть (tísnutʹ), Belarusian ці́снуць (císnucʹ), Polish cisnąć.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tỳsęťa, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tūˀsantis, from Proto-Indo-European *tuHsont-. Akin to English thousand.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tixъ.

parole.significato: to quieten down, to quiet down (to become quieter)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tixnǫti. By surface analysis, ти́х(ий) (týx(yj)) + -нути (-nuty). Compare Russian ти́хнуть (tíxnutʹ), Belarusian ці́хнуць (cíxnucʹ), Polish cichnąć, Czech tichnout.

parole.significato: to poke, to prod, to jab
parole.testo: Melnychuk posits inheritance from Proto-Slavic *tycati, a variant of *tykati. Compare Serbo-Croatian ти́цати, tícati.

parole.significato: silence, quietness, hush (the lack of any sound)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic тишина (tišina), from Proto-Slavic *tišina.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъkanь
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъkati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъkačь. By surface analysis, тка́ти (tkáty) + -ач (-ač).

From Old East Slavic тьло (tĭlo), from Proto-Slavic *tьlo, whence also Macedonian тло (tlo), Serbo-Croatian тло, Slovene tla (“floor”). Non-Slavic cognates include Latin tellūs (“the Earth”), Sanskrit तल (tala, “surface”), Old Irish talam (“earth”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъlěnъ. By surface analysis, тліти (tlity) + -нь f (-nʹ).

parole.significato: to wither away, to decay, to rot, to wear out, to go to ruin
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тлѣти (tlěti), from Old East Slavic тьлѣти (tĭlěti), from Proto-Slavic *tьlěti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *to.
Inherited from Old East Slavic товаръ (tovarŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tovarъ, borrowed from a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *tabar, borrowed from Sogdian 𐫕𐫁𐫀𐫡 (θbʾr).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tovariščь. Cognate with Russian това́рищ (továrišč), Belarusian тава́рыш (taváryš).

parole.significato: to crush, to pound, to mash, to pulp, to bray (using a pestle, masher, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian толчи́, товчи́ (tolčí, tovčí), from Old East Slavic тълчи (tŭlči), from Proto-Slavic *tьlťi, parallel to Proto-Slavic *telťi. Cognate with Belarusian таўчы́ (tawčý), dialectal Russian толчи́ (tolčí), Old Church Slavonic тлъщи (tlŭšti), Czech tlouct, Polish tłuc.

parole.significato: interpreter (one who conveys orally what a user of one language is saying or signing, in real time or shortly after tha…
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic тълмачь (tŭlmačĭ), from Proto-Slavic *tъlmačь. Doublet of тлума́ч (tlumáč), a borrowing from Polish tłumacz.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian толпа́ (tolpá), from Old East Slavic тълпа (tŭlpa), from Proto-Slavic *tъlpa.
From Proto-Slavic *tъlstъ. Doublet of тлу́стий (tlústyj), a borrowing from Polish.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *togъda.
Inherited from Old East Slavic тъ (tŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tas, from Proto-Indo-European *só, *séh₂, *tód (“this, that”).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian то́кмо (tókmo), from Old East Slavic токъмо, тъкъмо, тъкма (tokŭmo, tŭkŭmo, tŭkma), from Proto-Slavic *tъkъmo. Doublet of то́кма (tókma).

parole.significato: a fallow field used for grazing livestock
parole.testo: inherited from Proto-Slavic *telkti. Cognate with Russian толо́ка (tolóka), which also exists in southern and Siberian Russian dialects.

parole.significato: A collective effort to quickly clean up a place by members of a community.
parole.testo: inherited from Proto-Slavic *tolka. Cognate with Russian толо́ка (tolóka), which also exists in southern Russian and Ryazan dialects.

parole.significato: to tire, to exhaust, to wear out
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian томи́ти (tomíti), Old East Slavic томити (tomiti), from Proto-Slavic *tomiti. Cognate to Russian томи́ть (tomítʹ), Belarusian тамі́ць (tamícʹ), Old Church Slavonic томити (tomiti).
Inherited from Old East Slavic тънъкъ (tŭnŭkŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tьnъkъ.

Inherited from Old East Slavic тонути (tonuti), from Proto-Slavic *topnǫti. Cognate with Belarusian тану́ць (tanúcʹ), Russian тону́ть (tonútʹ), Bulgarian тъ́на (tắna), Serbo-Croatian то̀нути, Czech tonout, Polish tonąć.

Inherited from Old East Slavic топити (topiti, “to heat”), from Proto-Slavic *topiti (“to heat”). Cognate with Belarusian тапі́ць (tapícʹ), Russian топи́ть (topítʹ), Czech topit, Polish topić, Bulgarian топя́ (topjá), Serbo-Croatian то̀пити.

parole.significato: to drown (to kill by suffocating in water of other liquid)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic топити (topiti, “to drown”), from Proto-Slavic *topiti (“to drown”). Cognate with Belarusian тапі́ць (tapícʹ), Russian топи́ть (topítʹ), Czech topit, Polish topić.

parole.significato: poplar (any of various deciduous trees of the genus Populus)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *topoľa.
From Old East Slavic топоръ (toporŭ, “poleaxe”), from Proto-Slavic *toporъ. Further etymology is disputed.
Inherited from Old East Slavic търгъ (tŭrgŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tъrgъ.

parole.significato: to touch, to poke, to tap
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tьrkati.

parole.significato: to cause to flow, to cause to run, to flow
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *točiti (“to cause to flow, to cause to run”). Causative of текти́ (tektý, “to flow, to run”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъčьka.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tъčьnъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trava.

parole.significato: to etch (cut into a surface with an acid or other corrosive substance in order to make a pattern)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *traviti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tratiti.

parole.significato: to quake, to quiver, to shake, to shiver, to tremble
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trьmtěti, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *trem-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tretь.
From Proto-Slavic *trьje, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trьvožьnъ. By surface analysis, триво́га (tryvóha) + -ний (-nyj). Compare Russian трево́жный (trevóžnyj), Belarusian трыво́жны (tryvóžny), Polish trwożny (“timorous”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tri na desęte.

parole.significato: three times, thrice, on three occasions
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тро́йчи (trójči), from Old East Slavic троичи (troiči), from Proto-Slavic *trojьťi. By surface analysis, три (try) + -чі (-či). Cognate with Belarusian тро́йчы (trójčy). Compare Russian три́жды (tríždy), Old Church Slavonic тришьдꙑ (trišĭdy).

parole.significato: path, track (a trail for the use of, or worn by, pedestrians)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тропа́ (tropá), from Old East Slavic тропа (tropa), from Proto-Slavic *tropa.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trojь.
From Old East Slavic труба (truba), from Proto-Slavic *trǫba.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian трꙋдъ (trud), from Old East Slavic трꙋдъ (trudŭ), from Proto-Slavic *trudъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trudьnъ.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trupъ (“(tree) stump”), with this meaning still present in Czech and Polish trup, from Proto-Indo-European *truH-p. Perhaps related to Lithuanian traupus (“fragile,brittle”), Greek τρυπώ (trupṓ, “bore”). Compare Russian труп (trup), Belarusian труп (trup), Bulgarian труп
Inherited from Old Ruthenian трусити (trusiti), from Proto-Slavic *trǫsiti.
Inherited from Old East Slavic трудъ (trudŭ, “tinder fungus”), from Proto-Slavic *trǫdъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trǫtъ.
Inherited from Old East Slavic трꙋти (truti), from Proto-Slavic *truti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tręstì.

parole.significato: to ruffle, to tousle, to whiplash, to blow/toss around
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian трепати (trepati), from Old East Slavic трепати (trepati), from Proto-Slavic *trepati. The unexpected "і" in the root might come from the iterative forms such as трі́пати (trípaty) (See etymology 2) or -трі́пувати (-trípuvaty), where it is expected. Compare клепа́ти, клі

parole.significato: to flap, to jerk, to shake
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Slavic *trěpati, the iterative form of *trepati (See etymology 1).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *trěska.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тꙋга (tuha), from Old East Slavic тѫга (tǫga), from Proto-Slavic *tǫga.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tǫgъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tǫda.

parole.significato: to grieve, to mourn, to bewail, to sorrow, to eat one's heart out
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тꙋжи́ти (tužíti), from Old East Slavic тꙋжити, тѫжити (tužiti, tǫžiti), from Proto-Slavic *tǫžiti. By surface analysis, ту́га (túha) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тꙋкъ (tuk), from Old East Slavic тꙋкъ (tukŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tukъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тулъ (tul), from Old East Slavic тꙋлъ (tulŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tulъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian *тꙋли́ти (*tulíti), from Proto-Slavic *tuliti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tǫpъ.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тупи́ти (tupíti), from Proto-Slavic *tǫpiti. By surface analysis, туп- (tup-) + -ити (-yty).

parole.significato: to drive out, to drive away, to expel
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *turiti.
From Old East Slavic туто (tuto), тутъ (tutŭ, “here; thereto; herewith”), ту (tu, “there; thereto; then; here, herewith”), from Proto-Slavic *tuto, *tu.

parole.significato: to go out, to die down, die out (of light, fire)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tuxnǫti. Related to туши́ти (tušýty). Compare Russian ту́хнуть (túxnutʹ), Belarusian ту́хнуць (túxnucʹ).

parole.significato: to go bad, to go off, to go rotten, to spoil (putrefy or become inedible)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tǫxnǫti or *tuxnǫti, related to ту́хлий (túxlyj). Possibly related to Etymology 1. Compare Russian ту́хнуть (túxnutʹ), Belarusian ту́хнуць (túxnucʹ), Polish tęchnąć.

parole.significato: dark cloud, heavy cloud, rain cloud
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic туча (tuča), from Proto-Slavic *tǫča, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tenk- (“to contract”). Compare the Slavic Old Church Slavonic тѫча (tǫča), Russian ту́ча (túča), Polish tęcza and the Non-Slavic Gothic 𐌸𐌴𐌹𐍈𐍉𐌽 (þeiƕōn) and Old Norse þéttr.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тꙋчный (tučnyj), from Old East Slavic тꙋчьнъ (tučĭnŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tučьnъ. By surface analysis, тук (tuk) + -ий (-yj).

parole.significato: to extinguish, to put out, to quench
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian *тꙋшити (*tušiti) (see ꙋтꙋшити (utušiti)), from Proto-Slavic *tušiti.
From Proto-Slavic *dъxorь. Cognate with Belarusian тхор (txor), Russian хорь (xorʹ).
Inherited from Old East Slavic тьма (tĭma), from Proto-Slavic *tьma, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *timāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *temH-.

parole.significato: to dim, to darken, to obfuscate, to obscure, to eclipse
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian тмити (tmiti), from Proto-Slavic *tьmiti. By surface analysis, тьма (tʹma) + -ити (-yty).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tęgъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tęžarъ. Compare Belarusian цяжа́р (cjažár), Polish ciężar.
From Proto-Slavic *tędzati, *tęgati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tęťi.

parole.significato: to weigh down, to burden, to weighten
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tęžiti.
From Middle Ukrainian тѧжкий (tjažkyj), from Old East Slavic тѧжькъ (tęžĭkŭ), from Proto-Slavic *tęžьkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tingús, from Proto-Indo-European *tengʰ-.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тѧти, тꙗти (tjati, tjati), from Old East Slavic тѧти (tęti), from Proto-Slavic *tęti. Cognate with Belarusian цяць (cjacʹ), Polish ciąć, Old Novgorodian потѧти (potęti).
Inherited from Old Ruthenian тꙗтива (tjativa), from Old East Slavic тѧтива (tętiva), from Proto-Slavic *tętiva.
From Proto-Slavic *těkati (“to run”), iterative of *tekti (“to run, to flow”). Compare Polish uciekać.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tělo.
Inherited from Middle Ukrainian только (tolʹko), тольки (tolʹky), from Proto-Slavic *toliko. Compare Belarusian то́лькі (tólʹki).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *těmę.
From Proto-Slavic *těnь. Cognate with Russian тень (tenʹ), Belarusian цень (cjenʹ).

parole.significato: to scutch, to swingle (hemp, linen, flax)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *těpati, the iterative of Proto-Slavic *teti. Cognate with Slovak tepať, Polish ciepać, Bulgarian те́пам (tépam).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *těsnъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *těsto.

parole.significato: to cheer, to delight, to gladden, to please
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *těšiti.

parole.significato: in, at [with locative] (to express static position/location; the following word starts with a consonant)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic въ (vŭ), from Proto-Slavic *vъ(n), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥, zero-grade form of *h₁én.

From Proto-Slavic *ubьjьca. By surface analysis, уби́ти (ubýty, “to kill”) + -ця (-cja). Compare Bulgarian уби́йца (ubíjca), Macedonian убица (ubica), Old Church Slavonic убиїца (ubiica), Russian уби́йца (ubíjca), and Serbo-Croatian убица.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ubiti. Compare Russian уби́ть (ubítʹ), Bulgarian уби́я (ubíja), Polish ubić, Serbo-Croatian у̀бити/ùbiti, Slovene ubíti.
From Proto-Slavic *ubogъ. The noun is a nominalization of the adjective.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ugoda.
From Proto-Slavic *ǫgъrinъ, with -ець (-ecʹ) suffix. Cognates include Russian уго́рец (ugórec), Belarusian вуго́рац (vuhórac).

parole.significato: to hit, to strike, to smite (to deal a blow)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian уда́рити, вда́рити (udáriti, vdáriti), from Old East Slavic оударити (udariti), from Proto-Slavic *udariti, from Proto-Indo-European *derH-.

parole.significato: good luck, success (achievement of one's aim or goal)
parole.testo: From уда́ти(ся) (udáty(sja)) + -а (-a). Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dati, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dṓˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *dédeh₃ti (“to give”), whence English donate, date and data. Doublet of вда́ча (vdáča), back-formed from the "to be born with certain characteristics" meaning of the v

parole.significato: to coordinate, to bring into accordance, to harmonize, to make conform, to square
parole.testo: From у- (u-) + зго́дити (zhódyty), from Proto-Slavic *jьzgoditi. Compare Polish uzgodnić.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ukrasti. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + кра́сти (krásty). Compare Russian укра́сть (ukrástʹ), Belarusian укра́сці (ukrásci), Polish ukraść.

parole.significato: a territory or a land along the border of a country
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian украина (ukraina), from Old East Slavic украина (ukraina), from Proto-Slavic *ukràjina. By surface analysis, у (u) + край (kraj) + -ина (-yna).

parole.significato: to cover (to place something over or upon, as to conceal or protect)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ukryti. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + кри́ти (krýty). Compare Russian укры́ть (ukrýtʹ), Belarusian укры́ць (ukrýcʹ), Polish ukryć, Czech ukrýt, Slovak ukryť, Serbo-Croatian укрити/ukriti.
From у- (u-) + -куси́ти (-kusýty), from Proto-Slavic *kǫsiti. Compare Russian укуси́ть (ukusítʹ), Belarusian укусі́ць (ukusícʹ).
Inherited from Old East Slavic умъ (umŭ), from Proto-Slavic *umъ.
у- (u-) + ме́рти (mérty), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *merti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *umirati.

parole.significato: can, to be able to, to know how to
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *uměti.
Derived from Proto-Slavic *pęta (“heel”). See оп'я́ть (opʺjátʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫpyrь. Doublet of вампі́р (vampír).
Derived from Proto-Slavic *raziti. Cognates include Polish wrażenie, Belarusian уража́нне (uražánnje). By surface analysis, уражати (uražaty) + -ення (-ennja).

parole.significato: to hit, to strike, to wound
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ꙋразити (uraziti), from Old East Slavic ꙋразити (uraziti), from Proto-Slavic *uraziti. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + рази́ти (razýty).
From Proto-Slavic *uroďajь, whose middle part (*rodъ) yielded рід (rid). Cognates include Russian урожа́й (urožáj), Polish rodzaj.
Inherited from Old East Slavic урокъ (urokŭ, “agreement, condition”), from Proto-Slavic *urokъ, Proto-Slavic root *rok-.
From Proto-Slavic *urędъ. Cognate with Belarusian ура́д (urád).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian успѣхъ (uspěx), from Old East Slavic оуспѣхъ (uspěxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *uspěxъ. Cognate with Bulgarian успе́х (uspéh), Czech úspěch, Old Church Slavonic оуспѣхъ (uspěxŭ).

parole.significato: to establish, to determine, to fix, to set
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ustanoviti. Compare Russian установи́ть (ustanovítʹ), Polish ustanowić.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьśǫdu.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫtroba.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *utěxa.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *utěšьnъ. By surface analysis, уті́ш(ити) (utíš(yty)) + -ний (-nyj). Compare Belarusian уце́шны (ucjéšny), Polish ucieszny.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *učęstьnikъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *učęstь. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + часть (častʹ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *učenikъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *učiteľь. By surface analysis, учити (učyty) + -тель (-telʹ)

parole.significato: to teach (with person in accusative case + noun in genitive case or + infinitive)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *učiti.

Inherited from Old Ruthenian ꙋчꙋ́ти (učúti, “to hear, to feel, to sense”), from Old East Slavic ꙋчꙋти, ꙋчюти (učuti, učjuti, “to hear, to recognize”), from Proto-Slavic *učùti. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + чу́ти (čúty).

parole.significato: bootleg (the part of a boot that is above the instep)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *xoľeva.

parole.significato: to grab, to grasp, to seize, to snatch
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic хапати (xapati), from Proto-Slavic *xapati. Cognate with Belarusian хапа́ць (xapácʹ), Bulgarian ха́пя (hápja), Czech chápat, Polish chapać.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *xariti.
